A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COALA-PG research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original policy-training experiments and behavioral measurements on the iterated prisoner's dilemma and CleanUp-lite, including Figures 3–7.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on both games, revised benchmark results, and additional policy-fitting, initialization, gradient-balance, and cross-method interaction analyses.

M1.justification: The batched shaping objective, factorized long-context Hawk policies, and COALA-PG update are retained. The episode-separated gradient in v2's Theorem 3.1 already appears in v1's Equations 7 and 25. The new pseudocode documents TD/GAE calculations already indicated in v1, rather than establishing a new method component.

E1.justification: CleanUp-lite changes from a three-cell horizontal world with four actions to a 5×4 spatial grid with six actions, localized apples and dirt, and revised interaction dynamics (v1 Appendix A.1.2; v2 Appendix B.1.2). v2 also evaluates mixed COALA-PG/M-FOS populations, adding a distinct opponent-learning scenario.

E2.justification: LOLA-DICE, previously studied in analytical IPD experiments, joins the sampled sequence-policy comparisons in Figures 5–7 alongside M-FOS and batch-unaware COALA-PG. This substantially strengthens comparator coverage. New appendix analyses also compare learned policies with uniform random policies and tit-for-tat references.

E3.justification: Table 5 increases CleanUp mixed-pool training from 10,000 to 30,000 iterations and reduces both meta and naive populations from four to three. Tables 7–8 revise learning rates, discounts, and reward scaling. v2 adds cleaning discrepancy as a metric, initialization/fit protocols, and a gradient diagnostic using a meta-batch of 2,048.

E4.justification: Appendices C.1 and H add zero-determinant policy-fitting tests, defection and tit-for-tat initialization analyses, measurements of current-versus-future gradient contributions, and COALA-PG/M-FOS interaction experiments. These directly test mechanism and robustness questions beyond v1's existing training curves and behavioral analyses.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies eight-seed median/interquartile summaries for the initialization analyses in Figures 9–10 and 64-seed policy fitting in Figure 8. Retained figures preserve their 32-seed interquartile, 64-seed standard-error, and five-seed standard-deviation conventions. These disclosures do not establish increased runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: v2 revises Figure 3's analytical-IPD curves, adds LOLA comparison results, and replaces the CleanUp results under revised conditions. Appendix H.3 newly reports cooperative COALA-PG/M-FOS rewards of 0.850 ± 0.037 and 0.853 ± 0.017, respectively. Additional fitting, initialization, and gradient results expand the findings; changed CleanUp settings prevent interpreting its differences as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix D expands the policy-gradient proof into a trajectory-level derivation with a cross-trajectory cancellation argument, while retaining the central gradient and LOLA-relationship results. Appendix C.1 adds the mathematical zero-determinant parameterization used for fitting. The expanded proof contains a printed zero-expectation identity missing the gradient on log probability.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows superiority over previous methods to previous model-free methods and removes v1's claim of reaching cooperation for the first time in the sequential dilemma. The central unbiased, higher-derivative-free algorithm and cooperation-mechanism contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of mixed-pool equilibrium behavior, explains why learned strategies only approximate zero-determinant extortion, and discusses the timescale disadvantage that motivates excluding direct COALA-PG/LOLA co-training. The CleanUp interpretation shifts toward asymmetric cleaning against naive agents and fairer cleaning allocation between meta agents, replacing v1's specific cleaning-rate and percentage-gain discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Algorithm 1 substantially expand implementation guidance for batched lambda returns and method-specific GAE settings. v2 documents the revised CleanUp dynamics and hyperparameters and adds LOLA columns to Table 7. It removes value-normalization instructions and table rows; the Hawk architecture and software-library disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Aghajohari et al. (2024) on LOQA and Schulman et al. (2016) on GAE, removes several background and population-heterogeneity references, and narrows its comparative positioning to model-free methods. The principal relationships to M-FOS, Shaper, and LOLA remain. LOQA is cited, not experimentally evaluated.

P1.justification: Most of the narrative is retained, with targeted introduction and results rewrites. The LOLA explanation moves into Section 4.3, its estimator relationship moves to Appendix E, and implementation material becomes a separate Appendix A. These are localized rewrites and section moves within the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Figures 3–7 are redrawn, with substantially reorganized CleanUp panels, metrics, axes, and legends. v2 adds analysis Figures 8–12 and Algorithm 1; Figures 13–14 repeat main-text panels alongside additional diagnostics. Table 7 expands to include LOLA. Some revised captions are inconsistent with their plots, notably the cleaning-discrepancy direction in Figures 6B and 13B.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the paper through relevant LOLA-DICE sequence-policy comparisons, direct tests of the proposed cooperation mechanism, and explicit batched-advantage implementation guidance. These address important gaps in v1's comparator coverage and mechanistic validation, while the narrowed superiority claim better reflects the evidence. The spatial CleanUp redesign strengthens task demands but prevents direct cross-version score comparisons. New caption inconsistencies and a proof-notation error temper the improvement, particularly the reversed cleaning-discrepancy description in Figures 6B/13B, but do not outweigh the substantial evidential gains.
